target.title: fix(tdata): guard nil Document in media title/size helpers
target.body:
## Problem

A full/large `telecrawl import` from Telegram Desktop `tdata` crashes:

```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x2 addr=0x18 ...]
github.com/openclaw/telecrawl/internal/telegramdesktop.tdataMediaTitle(...)
	internal/telegramdesktop/tdata.go:764
github.com/openclaw/telecrawl/internal/telegramdesktop.(*tdataImportSession).convertMessage(...)
github.com/openclaw/telecrawl/internal/telegramdesktop.(*tdataImportSession).loadMessages.func1(...)
```

A small bounded import (a few dialogs) can miss the offending message; a full import reliably hits it.

## Root cause

`(*tg.MessageMediaDocument).Document` is a `tg.DocumentClass` interface that can be **nil** for some messages (e.g. expired/TTL documents, service-style media rows). `tdataMediaTitle` and `tdataMediaSize` call `media.Document.AsNotEmpty()` without a nil check, so the method dispatches on a nil interface and dereferences a nil pointer. The `!ok` return path can't help — the panic is on the call itself, before it returns.

## Fix

Guard `media.Document == nil` before `AsNotEmpty()` in both helpers, returning the zero value (`""` / `0`) consistent with the existing `!ok` handling. Two-line-per-site change; no behavior change for non-nil documents.

## Testing

- Added `TestTdataMediaDocumentNilDocument`, which feeds the exact crash input (`&tg.Message{Media: &tg.MessageMediaDocument{}}`). It panics on `main` and passes with the fix.
- `go test ./internal/telegramdesktop/` passes; `gofmt -l` and `go build ./...` are clean.
- Verified end-to-end on real data: a previously-crashing `telecrawl import` now archives **863 media messages with 0 panics**.
